Run covr on a package and upload the result to codecov.io

Source: R/codecov.R
codecov.Rd

Uploads coverage to Codecov with the current upload protocol, the one used by the Codecov CLI and the codecov/codecov-action GitHub Action. This takes two requests:

Usage

codecov(
  ...,
  coverage = NULL,
  base_url = "https://ingest.codecov.io",
  token = NULL,
  commit = NULL,
  branch = NULL,
  pr = NULL,
  flags = NULL,
  quiet = TRUE
)

Arguments

...

arguments passed to package_coverage()

coverage

an existing coverage object to submit, if NULL, package_coverage() will be called with the arguments from ...

base_url

the url coverage is uploaded to. The default is Codecov's upload API; change it for Codecov Enterprise. The former default "https://codecov.io" is the website, not the API, so it (and "https://app.codecov.io") is replaced by the default.

token

a codecov upload token, if NULL then following external sources will be checked in this order:

  1. the environment variable ‘CODECOV_TOKEN’. If it is empty, then

  2. package will look at directory of the package for a file codecov.yml. File must have codecov section where field token is set to a token that will be used.

If there is no token, the upload is sent without one, see the section “Tokens”.

commit

explicitly set the commit this coverage result object corresponds to. Is looked up from the service or locally if it is NULL.

branch

explicitly set the branch this coverage result object corresponds to, this is looked up from the service or locally if it is NULL.

pr

explicitly set the pr this coverage result object corresponds to, this is looked up from the service if it is NULL.

flags

A flag to use for this coverage upload see https://docs.codecov.com/docs/flags for details.

quiet

if FALSE, print the output of running the tests (see package_coverage(), which is called when coverage is NULL) and the coverage before submission.

Value

The response of Codecov to the request for an upload, invisibly: a list that includes url, the url of the upload on Codecov. If Codecov rejects either request, codecov() throws an error of class covr_codecov_error with the response of Codecov in its message, except when Codecov is rate limiting requests (HTTP 429) or is unavailable (HTTP 5xx), when it gives a warning of class covr_codecov_warning and returns NULL instead, so CI does not fail because of a transient Codecov problem.

Details

  1. POST <base_url>/upload/<git service>/<owner>::::<repo>/upload-coverage (for a repository in nested groups, owner/group/repo is owner:::group::::repo) tells Codecov about the commit, branch, pull request and CI job. The response contains a url for the upload on Codecov and a pre-signed location to send the coverage report to.

  2. PUT sends the report, covr's JSON coverage format (processed by Codecov as an R report), to that location. With branch coverage (see covr.branch_coverage), the report uses Codecov's generic JSON format instead, as the R format only takes line hits. A line with branches then has the number of its branches taken and the number of branches, e.g. "1/2", so Codecov shows it as partly covered unless all were taken.

If quiet is FALSE, the url of the upload on Codecov is printed after a successful upload.

The commit, branch, pull request, job, build URL and repository are looked up from the environment variables of the CI service, which is one of Jenkins, Travis, CircleCI, Drone, AppVeyor, GitLab CI, GitHub Actions or Google Cloud Build. Anywhere else, or for values the service does not provide, they are looked up from the local git repository in the working directory. The repository (owner/repo) and the git service (github, gitlab, bitbucket, ...) come from the CI service when it provides them, otherwise from the origin remote of the local git repository, otherwise the git service is assumed to be github.

Tokens

Codecov authenticates uploads with an upload token, passed in the Authorization header. Both the token of a repository and an organization (global) upload token, which is shared by all of an organization's repositories, can be used. The token is looked up as described for token. See https://docs.codecov.com/docs/codecov-tokens.

Without a token, Codecov only accepts uploads for public repositories, and only for an unprotected branch, which is a branch name with an owner prefix such as owner:branch. Pull requests from forks do not have access to the token as a CI secret, so on GitHub Actions, when there is no token, branch is NULL and the head repository of the pull request (the pull_request.head.repo.full_name of the event in GITHUB_EVENT_PATH) differs from GITHUB_REPOSITORY, codecov() uses the label of the head of the pull request, owner:branch, as the branch name, as codecov/codecov-action does. Pull requests from the same repository, other CI services and uploads from other branches use the plain branch name, so without a token Codecov rejects them unless the branch is already unprotected.

Alternative

Instead of uploading from R, write the coverage to a file and upload it with the codecov/codecov-action GitHub Action, or any other Codecov uploader. lcov() has no dependencies and writes lcov.info, which the action uploads without further configuration:

- name: Test coverage
  run: covr::lcov(covr::package_coverage())
  shell: Rscript {0}

- uses: codecov/codecov-action@v5
  with:
    token: ${{ secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN }}

cobertura() writes the Cobertura XML format, for which the xml2 package is needed.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
codecov(path = "test")
} # }
